name: GLM-5.3-Flash

sources.note: discussions read through the HF API

purpose: Z.ai states: the first natively multimodal model of the GLM-5 series, outperforming GLM-5.2 at one-tenth of the price and approaching Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agentic benchmarks; built for agentic engineering.

lineage.how_derived: newly trained base model (30T-token multimodal pre-training corpus), not derived from GLM-5.2

license.name: MIT
license.notes: LICENSE file in the repository read: standard MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Z.AI Co., Ltd: "to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies".

architecture.kind: hybrid linear + sparse attention MoE with manifold-constrained hyper-connections, multimodal
architecture.gguf_arch: glm5_next (Transformers name; llama.cpp name not verified)
architecture.attention: mostly linear attention layers with a DeepSeek-sparse-attention layer every fourth layer (layer_types in config.json; 64 heads, 64 KV heads)
architecture.why_this_design: Z.ai states: the first hybrid of sparse and linear attention in the GLM series sharply reduces long-context serving cost while preserving precise long-context retrieval; manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) improve scaling efficiency.

variants.notes: by NVIDIA, not by Z.ai; size not read

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 10% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 15% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM = 104 GB; about 23% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 29.6 GB VRAM plus 114 GB RAM = 144 GB; about 32% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

mac-16-24gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 12 GB)

mac-32gb.notes: estimate from the file size (93.1 GB) against the GPU share of docs/hardware (about 22 GB)

engine_support.notes: A llama.cpp user on 2026-09-24 still needed the unsloth glm5next branch (HF discussion unsloth/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF 22); whether mainline has it now is unchecked. Tona would need a new module (hybrid linear + DSA layers, mHC, 288 experts).

strengths: Vendor coding and agent numbers near the large closed models at 18 B active (vendor)
1 M context with a small KV cache: about 6 KB per token read from config.json (HF discussion 55)
MTP head gives draft acceptance 0.83 on agentic coding in a Vulkan run on a 128 GB unified-memory machine (HF unsloth discussion 27)
weaknesses: FIM tokens were removed: no fill-in-the-middle autocomplete (HF discussion 43)
Reasoning loops reported with some clients and chat templates (HF discussion 47)
93 GB at 1 bit: needs 24 GB VRAM + 96 GB RAM or more; quality of 1-bit quants unmeasured by us
No Artificial Analysis Coding Index entry found for the Flash model (only the larger GLM-5.3)
soft.behavior: Thinking budget via reasoning_effort low / high / max (default max); clear_thinking should be set true for chat.
best_for: agentic coding on 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class machines
very long context on a small KV budget
soft.maturity: Z.ai: large vendor with a GLM-5 technical report (arXiv 2602.15763); 6.4 M downloads of the main repo, 74 discussions, many community quantizations.

user_reports.summary: Reasoning loop on a trivial Kotlin task via opencode: 813K input tokens, no code; client dependent, fixed for one user by reverting the chat template
UD-IQ4_XS on 64 GB RAM + RTX 5090: about 250 tok/s prefill and 6 tok/s decode when streaming experts from two NVMe SSDs (custom patch); stock mmap offload 2.4 to 2.9 tok/s decode
Strix Halo 128 GB, llama.cpp Vulkan, MTP: about 29 tok/s decode on chat and 31 on coding, 74 to 83 % draft acceptance
FIM tokens removed, "useless" for completion compared to Qwen

tona_fit.reason: MIT (text verified), strongest vendor agent numbers of the Flash-class MoEs, small KV at 1 M context; fits the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class with a 1-bit quant (93 GB) and the 24 GB + 96 GB class marginally. Out of reach of the 16 GB + 64 GB reference class (93 GB against about 64 GB budget). Not offered for 16 GB.
blockers: Tona has no module for the hybrid linear/sparse attention layers and mHC (judged as engine support, not as model quality)
no FIM: not an autocomplete model
no independent score for the Flash model
